lesson.subtitle: Lesson 5 -- The Question You Did Not Prepare
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Adriana Cardoso Assunção | Lesson 5 -- The Question You Did Not Prepare

listenings.text: I coach executives for a living, and the thing people ask me about most is the question they did not prepare. Here is what I tell them. The silence after a hard question is never as long as it feels. Three seconds sounds like thirty inside your head and like nothing in the room. So use them. The second thing is that you are allowed to ask before you answer. Could you tell me which period you are asking about? That single sentence buys you time and makes the answer better, because half the hard questions in a meeting are hard only because they are vague. And the third thing: when you genuinely do not know, say it and give a date. I do not have that number with me, and I will send it to you by Friday. Nobody has ever lost credibility for that sentence.

Adriana, quick one before Thursday. I want you to know how that room works, because it is not the same as ours. The vice president asks one question and then says nothing for a long time. Do not fill the silence: he is waiting to see whether you add something you were not asked. The finance director interrupts, always, and never to attack you; he is checking whether you know the number well enough to keep going. And the head of operations asks the same question twice with different words. If you notice that, it is not a trap, it is how he thinks. One last thing: none of them will ask you anything about your English. That is a conversation only you are having.
